newsitem.title: USA: LTV Corp says steel demand seen strong in 97.
newsitem.headline: LTV Corp says steel demand seen strong in 97.

text.p: LTV Corp said Thursday it sees demand for steel remaining strong through the rest of the year but it is concerned about imports in the domestic market.

"We continue to expect the demand for steel to remain strong throughout 1997, but we remain concerned about the high level of imports flowing into the domestic market and the current strong dollar and its continued strengthening," said chairman and chief executive, David Hoag.
Hoag said the American Iron and Steel Institute reported January 1997 was the second highest monthly import total ever recorded in the U.S.
LTV said it expects to invest approximately $320 million in core integrated steel operations during 1997.
LTV said Thursday net income doubled to $26.8 million or $0.25 per share from $13.3 million, or $0.12 per share in the comparable 1996 period. A four percent increase in average
selling prices and four percent rise in shipments in the current reporting quarter were the primary reasons for an eight percent sales increase to $1.072 billion.

"Stronger prices and higher shipments improved our 1997 first quarter compared with the same period in 1996. We also benefited from the improved operating performance of our Cleveland Works. The continued strong demand for our products and high operating rates provided the opportunity to increase spot market prices on shipments after May 4, 1997," said Hoag.

Hoag said the Trico Steel joint venture successfully began operations and rolled its first coils at the end of March. "We anticipate Trico Steel will begin to contribute to LTV's income by the end of the year," he said.
